definition_zh: 夜晚；夜间；晚上；天黑；艰难时期
definition_en: the dark period between sunset and sunrise; the hours spent asleep; an evening given to an event; the coming of darkness; and a figurative time of trouble
core_image: 楼道灯灭下去，路灯把树影拉进屋角
scene: 楼道里的声控灯灭下去，窗外的路灯把树影拉进屋角。The city grows quiet at night.
sceneCN: 这里 night 是「夜晚」（第 1 个义项：日落到日出之间的黑暗时段）；句意为到了夜里，城市安静下来。图中可辨识物件：楼道灯、窗外路灯、树影。

derivatives.zh: 由 night 加 -ly 构成，义为「每夜的；每晚」
由 night 与 fall（落下）复合而成，义为「天黑；入夜」
由 mid（中间）与 night 复合而成，义为「午夜」
由 night 与 life 复合而成，义为「夜生活」

senses.title: The dark hours between sunset and sunrise
senses.definition: the period of darkness that begins at sunset and ends at sunrise
senses.definitionCN: 从日落开始到日出结束的那一段黑暗时间
senses.example: The streets are empty at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里街上空无一人。
senses.why: The Old English noun named the dark half of the day, and the word has kept that simple division of the clock ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的这个名词指的就是一天中黑暗的那一半，这个词至今仍守着钟面上这条简单的分界。

senses.title: A night spent asleep
senses.definition: the stretch of rest that a person gets between going to bed and waking
senses.definitionCN: 从上床到醒来之间那一段休息的时间
senses.example: She had a good night and woke up rested.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡了个好觉，醒来精神很好。
senses.why: Because the dark hours are the hours of sleep, the same word names the rest itself, so a good night is counted in hours slept rather than in anything seen.
senses.whyCN: 因为黑暗的那些小时正是睡觉的时辰，同一个词就用来指这段休息本身，所以「好的一夜」是按睡了多少小时来算，而不是按看见了什么。

senses.title: An evening given to an event
senses.definition: an evening set aside for a performance, a match or a social occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为演出、比赛或社交活动专门留出的那个晚上
senses.example: The opening night drew a full house.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜座无虚席。
senses.why: An event held after dark borrows the name of the time it fills, so the word can mean an evening handed over to a show or a game.
senses.whyCN: 天黑之后举办的活动会借用它所占据的时段的名字，所以这个词能指交给演出或比赛的那个晚上。

senses.title: The moment darkness falls
senses.definition: the point at which daylight ends and darkness comes down
senses.definitionCN: 白昼结束、黑暗降临的那一刻
senses.example: The light faded and night came down over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 光线退去，夜幕落到山谷上方。
senses.why: Since the same noun can name a period and its edge, it also marks the arrival of darkness, which is why a sentence can say that night came down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指一段时期，也能指它的边缘，所以它也标记黑暗的到来，这才有「夜幕落下」这样的句子。

senses.title: A time of gloom or trouble
senses.definition: a stretch of sorrow, fear or hardship felt as long and heavy as the dark hours
senses.definitionCN: 像黑夜一样漫长沉重的悲伤、恐惧或艰难时光
senses.example: The family went through a long night of worry before the results came.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来之前，这家人熬过了一段漫长的担忧。
senses.why: Darkness has long served as a figure for trouble, so a night can stand for any spell of fear or grief that feels as though the light will never return.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗自古就被用来比喻困境，所以 night 能指任何一段恐惧或悲伤的时光，仿佛光再也不会回来。

intro.en: Night is one of the oldest words English owns, an Old English noun still close to its Germanic shape and related to Latin nox.
intro.cn: night 是英语里最古老的词之一，这个古英语名词至今仍贴近它的日耳曼语形态，并与拉丁语 nox 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written nokwt- stands behind the word in many Indo-European languages, though scholars still argue about its exact shape.
items.cn: 许多印欧语系语言中这个词背后都有一个通常写作 nokwt- 的重构词根，不过学者对它的确切形态仍有争论。

items.en: The Germanic noun nahts gave Old English its word and also stands behind German Nacht.
items.cn: 日耳曼语名词 nahts 给了古英语这个词，也是德语 Nacht 的来处。

items.en: Niht named the dark part of the day and already formed compounds such as nihtlic, the ancestor of nightly.
items.cn: niht 指一天中黑暗的部分，并已构成 nihtlic 这样的复合词，那是 nightly 的前身。

items.en: Middle English kept the spellings niht and night, and the gh stopped being pronounced, leaving the long vowel heard today.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 niht 与 night 两种写法，后来 gh 不再发音，只留下今天听到的长元音。

items.en: Modern English uses night for the dark hours, for an evening event and for a time of sorrow, while the gh in the spelling is a silent relic.
items.cn: 现代英语用 night 指黑暗的时段、某个活动的晚上以及悲伤的时期，而拼写里的 gh 是一块沉默的遗迹。

entries.definition: The part of the day between afternoon and bedtime.

entries.definition: The darker stage of twilight, just before night.

entries.definition: The absence of light, the quality that defines the night.

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic noun of night that English kept almost unchanged, with a silent gh in the spelling and a large family of compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老的日耳曼语「夜」名词，英语几乎原样保留，拼写里有个不发音的 gh，周围还有一大族复合词。

normal.en: The gh in the spelling was once a throaty sound, and it went silent while the vowel lengthened.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 gh 曾经是一个喉咙里的音，后来它不响了，元音反而变长。

normal.en: Night and knight sound the same today, though one is a time and the other a rider.
normal.cn: night 与 knight 今天读音相同，但一个是时间，一个是骑马的人。

normal.en: The -ly of nightly means every night, the same ending that appears in daily and weekly.
normal.cn: nightly 里的 -ly 表示「每夜」，与 daily、weekly 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: Midnight is simply the middle of the night, built the same way as midday.
normal.cn: midnight 就是夜的正中，构词方式与 midday 一样。

normal.en: German Nacht and Latin nox descend from the same old root, which is why night turns up across so many languages.
normal.cn: 德语 Nacht 与拉丁语 nox 出自同一个古老词根，所以「夜」在许多语言里都有相似的影子。

abstract.en: A word for the dark half of the clock becomes a word for an evening out and for a spell of grief, because darkness measures time in more than one way.
abstract.cn: 一个指钟面暗半边的词，又成了外出的一晚和一段悲伤的时光，因为黑暗可以用不止一种方式计量时间。

abstract.en: Night and knight are twins in sound and strangers in meaning, a reminder that spelling keeps an old history the mouth has dropped.
abstract.cn: night 与 knight 声音上是双胞胎，意义上却是陌路人，提醒人拼写保存着口腔早已丢掉的旧历史。

abstract.en: Every night is both a period and a beginning, which is why the same noun can mean the dark hours and the moment they arrive.
abstract.cn: 每一个夜晚既是一段时期，也是一个开端，所以同一个名词既能指黑暗的时段，也能指它降临的那一刻。

definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighteenth; one of nineteen equal parts; the nineteenth day of a month
core_image: 一排十九级台阶，最后一级上放着一支点亮的蜡烛
scene: 黄昏的走廊里排着十九级台阶，最后一级上放着一支点亮的蜡烛。Her birthday falls on the nineteenth of May.
sceneCN: 这里是「某月的十九日」（第 3 个义项：一个月里编号为十九的那天）；句意为她的生日在五月十九日。图中可辨识物件：十九级台阶、蜡烛、走廊的扶手。

pos.zh: 十九分之一；（某月的）十九日

derivatives.zh: 由 nineteenth 加 -ly 构成，义为「第十九（用于列举）」
由 nineteenth 与 century 复合而成，义为「十九世纪的」

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighteenth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighteenth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第十八之后的数
senses.example: She finished nineteenth in a field of forty runners.
senses.exampleCN: 她在四十名跑者中排名第十九。
senses.why: Nineteenth is nine plus -teen plus -th: the teen ending marks ten added to a unit, and the ordinal ending marks a place in a line, so the word counts the spot just before twenty.
senses.whyCN: nineteenth 是 nine 加 -teen 再加 -th：-teen 表示十加个位数，序数词尾 -th 标出它在一列中的位置，所以这个词数的正是紧挨二十之前的那一位。

senses.title: One of nineteen equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nineteen equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成十九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A nineteenth of the profit went to the local fund.
senses.exampleCN: 利润的十九分之一拨给了本地基金。
senses.why: The same ordinal ending that ranks an item also cuts a whole into that many pieces, so a nineteenth is the share created by dividing by nineteen.
senses.whyCN: 标出名次的序数词尾，同时也把整体切成同样多的份，所以 a nineteenth 就是被十九除开之后得到的那一份。

senses.title: The nineteenth day of a month
senses.definition: the day of a month numbered nineteenth, used mostly in dates
senses.definitionCN: 一个月中编号为十九的那一天，多用于日期
senses.example: The office reopens on the nineteenth.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室在十九日重新开放。
senses.why: Dates are a list of days, so the ordinal that ranks an item in a series doubles as the name of a particular day; English drops the noun day and lets the ordinal stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 日期本身就是一串日子，因此在序列里排位的序数词也兼作某一天的名称；英语省掉 day，直接让序数词单独站立。

intro.en: Nineteenth is a native English compound of nine, the teen ending and the ordinal ending, and it belongs to the Germanic number words that English never borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nineteenth 是英语本土的复合词，由 nine、表示十几的词尾和序数词尾构成，属英语从未向拉丁语借用的日耳曼数词。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构出来的；它的确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的词。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine, and it stands at the base of nineteen, ninety and nineteenth alike.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是 nineteen、ninety 与 nineteenth 共同的底座。

items.en: The ending -tīene or -tēne meant ten more, so nigontīene counted nine beyond ten.
items.cn: 词尾 -tīene 或 -tēne 表示「又多十」，因此 nigontīene 数的是十之后再添九。

items.en: The ordinal added the -tha ending used for ranking, producing the ancestor of nineteenth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -tha，形成 nineteenth 的祖先。

items.en: Modern English spells the compound nineteenth and uses it for rank, for a nineteenth part, and for the nineteenth day of a month.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词写作 nineteenth，用来表示名次、十九分之一，以及某月的十九日。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its cardinal, tens and ordinal forms; the near-meaning group places nineteenth between its neighbours on the counting line.
note.cn: 形近组沿着同一个「九」的底座，收它的基数、十位与序数形式；近义组把 nineteenth 放回计数序列，看它前后相邻的词。

entries.definition: The cardinal before nineteenth, built on the same nine and teen elements.
entries.definitionCN: nineteenth 之前的基数词，由同样的 nine 与 teen 成分构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal for ninety, formed from ninety with the same -th ending used here.
entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，由 ninety 加同一个 -th 词尾构成。

entries.definition: The ordinal for nine, the smallest member of the same ordinal family.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，是同一序数词族里最小的一员。

entries.definition: The tens form of nine, built with the -ty ending rather than -teen.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 词尾而不是 -teen。

entries.definition: The ordinal immediately before nineteenth in the same counting line.
entries.definitionCN: 同一计数序列中紧挨在第十九之前的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal immediately after nineteenth, closing the teens.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第十九之后的序数词，为十几这一段的结尾。

entries.definition: The ending shared by the numbers thirteen to nineteen, the group nineteenth belongs to.
entries.definitionCN: 十三到十九共用的词尾，正是 nineteenth 所属的那一组。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position in a series, the class to which nineteenth belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 标出序列中位置的数词，是 nineteenth 所属的类别。

normalIntro.en: The word stacks three small pieces of English counting, a unit, a ten and a rank ending, and each piece explains one of its uses.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把英语计数的三个小零件叠在一起：一个个位数、一个「十」和一个表名次的词尾，每个零件都解释了它的一种用法。

normal.en: Nineteen is nine plus ten, so nineteenth is the ordinal of the number that sits one step before twenty.
normal.cn: 十九就是九加十，所以 nineteenth 是紧挨二十之前那个数的序数形式。

normal.en: The -teen ending means ten added to a unit, while -ty in ninety means tens; nineteenth follows the first pattern.
normal.cn: 词尾 -teen 表示十加个位数，而 ninety 里的 -ty 表示若干个十；nineteenth 走的是前一种模式。

normal.en: The -th ending turns a count into a rank, the same ending heard in fourth and twentieth.
normal.cn: 词尾 -th 把计数变成名次，和 fourth、twentieth 里听到的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: A nineteenth can also be a part, because dividing a whole by nineteen creates nineteen equal shares.
normal.cn: a nineteenth 也可以是一份，因为把整体按十九去分，就得到十九个相等的份。

normal.en: Dates use the bare ordinal, so on the nineteenth means on the nineteenth day of the month.
normal.cn: 日期直接用序数词，所以 on the nineteenth 就是在这个月的第十九天。

abstract.en: Nineteen is the last number before the round twenty, so its ordinal always sounds like a step just short of a clean boundary.
abstract.cn: 十九是整数二十之前的最后一个数，所以它的序数听起来总像差一步就到干净边界。

abstract.en: The same word can rank a runner, cut a cake into nineteen pieces and name a day, because English lets one ordinal do the work of position, fraction and date.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以给跑者排名、把蛋糕切成十九份、还给某一天命名，因为英语让一个序数词同时承担位置、分数和日期三件事。

abstract.en: Counting words are the skeleton of a language, and nineteenth shows how a unit, a ten and a rank ending stack into one short word.
abstract.cn: 计数词是语言的骨架，而 nineteenth 展示了「一个个位数、一个十、一个名次词尾」如何叠成一个短词。

examples.en: She finished nineteenth in a field of forty runners.
examples.cn: 她在四十名跑者中排名第十九。

examples.en: A nineteenth of the profit went to the local fund.
examples.cn: 利润的十九分之一拨给了本地基金。

examples.en: The office reopens on the nineteenth.
examples.cn: 办公室在十九日重新开放。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈恩婷丝」——数到十九级台阶，最后一级亮着蜡烛；nineteenth 就是第十九。

root: 古英语 nigon（九）加 -tīene（十）构成 nigontīene（十九），再加序数词尾 -tha 成为 nigontēontha；现代英语写作 nineteenth，属日耳曼语系本土数词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rank just before twenty; the same form then serves as a nineteenth part and as the nineteenth day of a month.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是紧挨二十之前的一个名次；同一个形式再兼作十九分之一和某月的十九日。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of nineteen steps with a lit candle standing on the last one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排十九级台阶，最后一级上立着一支点亮的蜡烛。

branches.en: a runner crossing the line in nineteenth place
branches.cn: 跑者以第十九名冲过终点线

branches.en: the last step before a round twentieth
branches.cn: 紧挨整数二十之前的最后一级

branches.en: a cake cut into nineteen equal slices
a share of the profit marked on a calendar page
branches.cn: 利润的一份被记在日历的某一页上

branches.en: a notice on the door announcing the nineteenth
branches.cn: 门上贴出十九日重开的通知

intro.en: The word is assembled from the Old English nine, the teen suffix that adds ten, the ordinal ending and the English endings it still takes.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的「九」、表示「再加十」的词尾、序数词尾，以及它至今仍在使用的英语词尾组装而成。

latinIntro.en: English nine descends from the same ancient Indo-European numeral as Latin novem, so the Latin forms are cognates for comparison, not the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 同出古老的原始印欧语数词，因此下列拉丁形式只供对照，并不是英语这个词的来源。

definition_zh: 九十；九十年代；九十多岁
definition_en: the number equal to nine times ten; also the years of a decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine, and ages in that range
core_image: 摊主把硬币十个一摞码成九摞，最后一摞刚好压到旧布的边缘
scene: 清晨的旧货市场里，摊主把硬币十个一摞码成九摞，最后一摞正好压到旧布的边缘。The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
sceneCN: 这里是「九十」这个数目（第 1 个义项：九乘十）；句意为那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。图中可辨识物件：硬币摞、旧布边、旧钟。

derivatives.zh: 由 ninety 加序数词尾 -th（拼作 -tieth）构成，义为「第九十」
由 ninety 与 odd 复合构成，义为「九十好几的」

senses.title: The number nine times ten
senses.definition: the number equal to nine groups of ten, written with the digits nine and zero
senses.definitionCN: 等于九组十的数，写作九与零
senses.example: The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。
senses.why: Ninety is a native Germanic tens word: nine plus an ending that means a group of ten, so the word itself says nine tens rather than naming a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninety 是日耳曼语本土的十位词：九加上表示「一组十」的词尾，所以这个词自己就在说「九个十」，而不是给一个新数量另起名字。

senses.title: The decade numbered ninety to ninety-nine
senses.definition: the period of ten years in a century numbered from ninety to ninety-nine, usually written the nineties
senses.definitionCN: 一个世纪里编号从九十到九十九的那十年，通常写作 the nineties
senses.example: The building was put up in the nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼建于九十年代。
senses.why: A century is a run of hundred years, so the last ten can be named by the tens word that opens them; English uses the plural to mean the whole span, not one year.
senses.whyCN: 一个世纪是一百年的长串，最后十年可以用开启它的那个十位数来命名；英语用复数表示整段，而不是单独一年。

senses.title: An age between ninety and ninety-nine
senses.definition: the ages from ninety to ninety-nine, especially in the phrase in one's nineties
senses.definitionCN: 从九十岁到九十九岁之间的年龄，尤用于 in one's nineties 这一说法
senses.example: She is still writing in her nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她九十多岁仍在写作。
senses.why: An age range is also a span of ten, so the same plural serves for a person's tenth decade; being in the nineties means living inside that stretch.
senses.whyCN: 年龄区间同样是一段十岁，于是同一个复数也用来指人生的第十个十年；in one's nineties 就是活在那一段里。

intro.en: Ninety is one of the native tens numerals English builds by joining a unit to an ending for a group of ten, and its plural later took on the meaning of a decade.
intro.cn: ninety 是英语本土的十位数之一，由个位数加表示「一组十」的词尾拼成；它的复数后来又承担了「十年」的意思。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants, and the exact shape of that base is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的，这个底座的确切形状存疑。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of both the tens numeral and the ordinal.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是这个十位数与对应序数词的共同底座。

items.en: The ending -tig meant a group of ten, so nigontig said nine tens in one word.
items.cn: 词尾 -tig 表示「一组十」，因此 nigontig 用一个词说出九个十。

items.en: Middle English kept the tens numeral as nineti and used the plural for groups and repeated counts.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个十位数保留为 nineti，并用复数表示多组或反复计数。

items.en: Modern English uses ninety as a number and the nineties for a decade, an age range and temperatures near ninety.
items.cn: 现代英语用 ninety 表示数目，用 the nineties 表示十年、年龄区间以及九十度上下的温度。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps to words built on the same nine base; the near-meaning group puts ninety on the same number line as its neighbours and the ten-year span it names.
note.cn: 形近组只收建在同一个「九」底座上的词；近义组把 ninety 放回同一条数轴，与相邻的数以及它所代表的那段十年对照。

entries.definition: The ordinal built on ninety with the -th ending.
entries.definitionCN: 在 ninety 上加 -th 词尾构成的序数词。

entries.definition: The unit numeral beneath ninety, the nine in nine tens.
entries.definitionCN: ninety 之下的个位数词，就是九个十里的那个九。

entries.definition: The teen form of nine, using the other ten pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十几形式，用的是另一种「十」的模式。

entries.definition: The ordinal of nine, sharing the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 九的序数词，共享同一个底座。

entries.definition: The tens number ten below ninety.
entries.definitionCN: 比九十低十的十位数。

entries.definition: The round number above ninety, the next landmark on the scale.
entries.definitionCN: 九十之上的整数，是尺度上的下一个地标。

entries.definition: A group of twenty, an older English way of counting in tens and twenties.
entries.definitionCN: 一组二十，是英语较早按十与二十计数的说法。

entries.definition: A period of ten years, the unit that makes the nineties a span.
entries.definitionCN: 十年的一段时间，正是让 nineties 成为一段的单位。

normalIntro.en: The word is nine plus an old ending for a group of ten, and its plural extends the number into a decade and a decade of a life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」加上一个表示「一组十」的古老词尾，它的复数形式又把数目伸向十年和人生的十年。

normal.en: Ninety is nine tens: nine plus the -ty ending, which came from an Old English word for a group of ten.
normal.cn: 九十就是九个十：九加上 -ty 词尾，这个词尾来自古英语里表示「一组十」的词。

normal.en: The same base gives nineteen with -teen and ninety with -ty, so the two endings tell you whether ten is added or multiplied.
normal.cn: 同一个底座加上 -teen 得到 nineteen，加上 -ty 得到 ninety，两个词尾告诉你十是被加还是被乘。

normal.en: Ninetieth is ninety plus -th, the ordinary way English turns a count into a rank.
normal.cn: ninetieth 是 ninety 加 -th，正是英语把计数变成名次的寻常做法。

normal.en: The plural nineties names both a decade and an age range, because each is a block of ten years.
normal.cn: 复数 nineties 既指一个年代，也指一个年龄段，因为两者都是一块十年的长度。

normal.en: Ninety-nine is the last number before the next hundred, so ninety sits at the top of the two-digit tens.
normal.cn: 九十九是下一个百之前的最后一个数，所以九十站在两位数十位数的顶端。

abstract.en: A number made by stacking nine groups of ten carries its own explanation inside it, which is why tens words feel so transparent.
abstract.cn: 一个由九个十堆起来的数，把自己的解释藏在词里，所以十位词读起来总显得透明。

abstract.en: The jump from number to decade costs no new word, because a decade is simply ten counted one after another.
abstract.cn: 从数目跳到年代不需要另造新词，因为一整个年代不过是把十一个个数下去。

abstract.en: Ninety marks the last stretch before a hundred, the point where counting starts to feel like a rounder kind of arithmetic.
abstract.cn: 九十标出百之前的最后一段，正是计数开始变得像整块算术的地方。

examples.en: The old clock still keeps time after ninety years.
examples.cn: 那座旧钟走了九十年仍在计时。

examples.en: The building was put up in the nineties.
examples.cn: 这栋楼建于九十年代。

examples.en: She is still writing in her nineties.
examples.cn: 她九十多岁仍在写作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈恩提」——硬币十个一摞，码到第九摞正好压住布边；ninety 就是九十。

root: 古英语 nigon（九）加 -tig（一组十）构成 nigontig（九十），中古英语作 nineti；复数 nineties 又扩展为年代与年龄段。

sensesIntro.en: The core is nine groups of ten; the plural then opens into a decade of years and a decade of a person's life.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是九组十；复数形式再分出年份的十年与人生的第十个十年。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: nine stacks of ten coins meeting the edge of an old cloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：九摞各十枚的硬币正好压到旧布的边缘。

branches.en: nine stacks of ten coins meeting the edge of a cloth
branches.cn: 九摞硬币正好压到布边

branches.en: a clock dial passing ninety years
a city skyline built in the nineties
branches.cn: 九十年代建起的城市天际线

branches.en: a writer still working in her nineties
branches.cn: 九十多岁仍在写作的人

branches.en: the same plural covering years and years of a life
branches.cn: 同一个复数既指年份，也指人生的年岁

intro.en: The word joins the Old English nine to the ending for a group of ten, and its plural and ordinal forms are ordinary English building on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词把古英语的「九」接到表示一组十的词尾上，它的复数与序数形式都是在这座底座上的寻常英语构词。

latinIntro.en: English nine shares an ancient Indo-European origin with Latin novem, so the Latin numerals below are cognates for comparison, not borrowing sources.
latinIntro.cn: 英语的 nine 与拉丁语 novem 共享原始印欧语来源，因此下面的拉丁数词只是同源对照，不是借用来源。

items.meaning: decades or ages in the nineties

definition_zh: 第九；九分之一
definition_en: the ordinal number that comes after the eighth; one of nine equal parts
core_image: 九级台阶的最上面放着一块小小的铜牌，牌上刻着一条横线
scene: 楼道里的九级台阶被擦得很亮，最上面一级放着一块小小的铜牌。He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
sceneCN: 这里是「第九层」（第 1 个义项：序数第九）；句意是他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。图中可辨识物件：九级台阶、铜牌、楼道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 ninth 加 -ly 构成，义为「第九（用于列举）」
ninth 的基数形式，古英语 nigon 一路传下来，义为「九」

senses.title: The ordinal number after the eighth
senses.definition: the number that comes after the eighth in a counted series
senses.definitionCN: 在计数序列中排在第八之后的数
senses.example: He lives on the ninth floor of a narrow building.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在一栋窄楼房的第九层。
senses.why: Ninth is nine plus the old ordinal ending -th, the same ending that makes fourth from four; the ending marks a place in a line, not a new quantity.
senses.whyCN: ninth 是 nine 加古老的序数词尾 -th，和 four 变 fourth 用的是同一个词尾；这个词尾标出的是一列中的位置，而不是一个新数量。

senses.title: One of nine equal parts
senses.definition: each of the nine equal parts into which a whole can be divided
senses.definitionCN: 把整体分成九等份时其中的一份
senses.example: A ninth of the students chose the longer course.
senses.exampleCN: 九分之一的学生选了那门较长的课程。
senses.why: The ordinal ending also cuts: a ninth is what one gets when a whole is split nine ways, which is why the rank word and the fraction word look identical.
senses.whyCN: 这个序数词尾同时也起切割作用：把整体分成九份，得到的就是 a ninth，所以表示名次的词和表示分数的词长得一模一样。

intro.en: Ninth is the ordinal of nine, formed in Old English by a unit numeral plus the ending that marks rank, then trimmed into its modern spelling.
intro.cn: ninth 是九的序数词，在古英语里由个位数词加表名次的词尾构成，后来缩减成今天的拼写。

items.en: The Germanic numeral for nine is reconstructed from its later descendants; its exact shape is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的「九」是依据后来的后代形式重构的；确切形状只是重构，不是有记录的形式。

items.en: Nigon was the Old English word for nine and the base of the whole ordinal family.
items.cn: nigon 是古英语的「九」，也是整个序数词族的底座。

items.en: The ordinal added the -þa ending used for ranking, giving the ancestor of ninth.
items.cn: 序数形式加上用于排位的词尾 -þa，形成 ninth 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English shortened and respelled the word as ninthe, and the modern consonant pattern was already visible.
items.cn: 中古英语把词形缩短并改写为 ninthe，现代的辅音格局那时已经看得出来。

items.en: Modern English fixes the spelling ninth and uses it both for rank and for the fraction one of nine equal parts.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写固定为 ninth，并用它同时表示名次与九等份中的一份。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same nine base through its teen, tens, ordinal and adverb forms; the near-meaning group places ninth between its neighbours and next to the idea of a fraction.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一个「九」的底座，收十几、十位、序数与副词形式；近义组把 ninth 放到相邻序数之间，并与分数的概念放在一起。

entries.definition: The teen form of nine, built with -teen instead of the ordinal ending.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十几形式，用 -teen 而不是序数词尾构成。

entries.definition: The tens form of nine, built with -ty.
entries.definitionCN: 九的十位形式，用 -ty 构成。

entries.definition: The adverb built on ninth with -ly, used in lists.
entries.definitionCN: ninth 加 -ly 构成的副词，用于列举。

entries.definition: The ordinal for ninety, part of the same -th family.
entries.definitionCN: 九十的序数词，属同一 -th 词族。

entries.definition: The ordinal just before ninth in the same line.
entries.definitionCN: 同一序列中紧挨在第九之前的序数词。

entries.definition: The ordinal just after ninth, closing the single digits.
entries.definitionCN: 紧挨在第九之后的序数词，为个位数的结尾。

entries.definition: A number word that marks position, the class of ninth.
entries.definitionCN: 标出位置的数词，ninth 所属的类别。

entries.definition: A part of a whole, the kind of quantity one ninth expresses.
entries.definitionCN: 整体中的一份，正是九分之一所表达的量。

normalIntro.en: The word is nine wearing the ordinary English rank ending, and the same form serves as a rank and as a share because the ending does both jobs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「九」披上寻常的英语名次词尾；同一个形式既是名次也是一份，因为这个词尾兼做两件事。

normal.en: Nine plus -th is the same pattern as four plus -th; ninth is the ninth place, not a new quantity.
normal.cn: 九加 -th 和四加 -th 是同一个模式；ninth 是第九个位置，不是一个新数量。

normal.en: The old ordinal ending survives in modern English even though the Old English spelling has been trimmed away.
normal.cn: 古老的序数词尾在现代英语里仍然活着，尽管古英语的拼写已经被削掉。

normal.en: Ninth also divides: cut a whole into nine equal pieces and each piece is a ninth.
normal.cn: ninth 也用来分：把整体切成九个等份，每一份就是一个 ninth。

normal.en: Ninthly is built on ninth with -ly, the way English turns an ordinal into a list marker.
normal.cn: ninthly 是在 ninth 后加 -ly 造出来的，英语就这样把序数变成列举时的标记。

normal.en: Dates and floors use the bare ordinal, so on the ninth or the ninth floor needs no extra noun.
normal.cn: 日期和楼层都用光秃秃的序数词，所以 on the ninth 或 the ninth floor 不用再加名词。

abstract.en: Ninth is the last single-digit ordinal, so it sounds like the end of the simplest counting line.
abstract.cn: ninth 是个位数里的最后一个序数词，听起来像最简单那条计数线的收尾。

abstract.en: The word barely changed shape across a thousand years, which makes it a small fossil of how English counts.
abstract.cn: 这个词一千年里形状几乎没变，因此它是英语如何计数的一小块化石。

core_image: 一间本该坐满人的屋子，椅子全是空的
scene: 会议室的门开着，桌上的杯子还冒着热气，可一圈椅子全是空的。Nobody came to the meeting, so the chairs stayed empty all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 nobody 是「没有一个人」（第 1 个义项：在场的人一个也没有）；句意为没有人来开会，椅子整个下午都空着。图中可辨识物件：冒热气的杯子、空椅子、开着的门。

senses.title: Not a single person
senses.definition: not one person; no person at all, used when the number of people present is zero
senses.definitionCN: 一个人也没有；表示在场人数为零
senses.example: Nobody was waiting at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 车站里没有一个人在等。
senses.why: The word welds the negator no onto body, so it denies not an action but the very existence of a human figure in the scene.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把否定词 no 焊在 body 上，否定的不是某个动作，而是场景里是否存在一个具体的人。

senses.title: A person of no importance
senses.definition: an ordinary or unimportant person, especially one without fame or influence
senses.definitionCN: 普通而不重要的人，尤指没有名声或影响力的人
senses.example: He was a nobody before the film made him famous.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部电影让他出名之前，他只是个无名小卒。
senses.why: Once nobody rules out any important figure, the phrase can be turned into a countable noun that names the missing importance itself.
senses.whyCN: 当 nobody 排除了任何重要人物之后，这个说法就能变成可数名词，直接指那份缺失的分量。

senses.title: No person except
senses.definition: used in the pattern nobody but to mean no person other than the one named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 nobody but 结构，表示除了提到的这个人之外没有别人
senses.example: Nobody but the guard saw him leave.
senses.exampleCN: 除了门卫，没有人看见他离开。
senses.why: The negator still empties the scene of people, and but then names the single exception hidden inside that emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 否定词仍然把场景里的人清空，but 随后点出藏在这片空无之中的唯一例外。

intro.en: Nobody is an English compound of the negator no and the noun body, first recorded in the fourteenth century and not borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: nobody 是英语否定词 no 与名词 body 的复合，最早见于十四世纪，并非借自拉丁语。

items.en: The Old English negator nā meant not or no, and it is the ancestor of modern no.
items.cn: 古英语否定词 nā 意为「不、没有」，是现代 no 的前身。

items.en: Bodig meant the body, the physical frame of a person, and became modern body.
items.cn: bodig 指身体、人的躯体，后来演变为 body。

items.en: In the fourteenth century the two words were joined as nobody, a pronoun meaning no person.
items.cn: 十四世纪这两个词合成 nobody，作代词表示「没有人」。

items.en: Writers began using a nobody as a countable noun for a person of no account.
items.cn: 到了十六、十七世纪，作家开始用 a nobody 这个可数名词，指无足轻重的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps both uses and adds the plural nobodies for several unimportant people.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两种用法，并加上复数 nobodies 来指多个无足轻重的人。

definition_zh: 点头；点头示意；打盹；致意
definition_en: to move the head quickly down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement, and also to fall asleep briefly
core_image: 下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位
scene: 散会后，他没有开口，只朝门口等着的同事低了下头，随即转身离开。He gave her a brief nod and walked out of the room.
sceneCN: 这里 nod 是「点头示意」（第 1 个义项：以点头表示问候或同意）；句意为他朝她轻轻点了下头，就走出了房间。图中可辨识物件：半开的会议室门、走廊里的同事、手里的文件。

derivatives.zh: nod 加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「点头的；（花枝等）低垂的」

senses.title: To move the head down and up as a greeting or sign of agreement
senses.definition: to move the head quickly down and up, especially to greet someone or to show that you agree
senses.definitionCN: 快速地把头低下再抬起，尤用于问候别人或表示同意
senses.example: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。
senses.why: A nod is the smallest visible yes: the head dips and returns, and the whole body quietly accepts what has just been said.
senses.whyCN: 点头是最小的一个看得见的「是」：头低下去又回来，整个身体就安静地接受了刚才听到的话。

senses.title: To fall asleep briefly, especially when you should stay awake
senses.definition: to begin to sleep accidentally for a short time, often while sitting or listening
senses.definitionCN: 在不该睡的时候不小心睡着一小会儿，常发生在坐着或听讲时
senses.example: He nodded off during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。
senses.why: The same drooping motion that signals sleepiness ends in a real loss of attention, so the verb stretches from a greeting to a head that falls forward and stays down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个耷拉下去的动作本是困意的信号，最后却变成真正的走神，于是词义从问候扩到「头垂下去、撑不住睡着」。

senses.title: A single quick movement of the head
senses.definition: a single quick movement of the head down and back up, used as a signal
senses.definitionCN: 头快速低下再抬起的一次动作，用作某种信号
senses.example: She answered with a quick nod.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻点了一下头作为回答。
senses.why: When the gesture is seen as an event rather than an act, the same word becomes a noun that counts each dip of the head.
senses.whyCN: 当这个手势被看成一件发生的事，而不是一个动作时，同一个词就变成名词，数得清每一次低头。

senses.title: An act of acknowledgement or tribute
senses.definition: a gesture, design or remark that openly acknowledges or honours someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 公开表示认可或致敬的动作、设计或言辞
senses.example: The new building is a nod to the town's fishing past.
senses.exampleCN: 这座新建筑是在向小镇的渔业历史致意。
senses.why: A small gesture of recognition is enough to say that something deserves respect, so the word widens from the head movement to any quiet sign of approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个很小的致意动作，就足以说明某样东西值得尊重；于是词义从头部的动作扩展到任何安静的认可。

intro.cn: nod 最早记录于中古英语，更早的来源不确定；一般认为它是模仿动作的表达性词语，而不是借自拉丁语。

items.en: Nodden meant to make a quick bowing movement of the head, close to the modern gesture.
items.cn: nodden 意为把头快速低一下，和现代的手势已经很接近。

items.en: The word is attested in writing from the fourteenth century with the sense of the head movement.
items.cn: 这个词从十四世纪起见于书面记录，表示头部的这一动作。

items.en: The phrase nod off appears for falling asleep in a chair, adding the sleep sense to the family.
items.cn: nod off 这个说法出现，用于在椅子上睡着，为这个词族添上了「打盹」的义项。

items.en: Modern English keeps the verb, uses the noun for the gesture, and extends a nod to to mean tribute.
items.cn: 现代英语保留动词，用名词指这个动作，并把 a nod to 扩展为致敬之意。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on nod, plus one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers other small signals and other words for light sleep.
note.cn: 形近组收由 nod 构成的形式，另收一个只是长得像的词；近义组收其他细小的示意动作，以及表示浅睡的词。

entries.definition: The present participle and adjective of nod, also used of drooping plants.
entries.definitionCN: nod 的现在分词兼形容词，也用于花枝低垂。

entries.definition: A person who nods, often repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 点头的人，常指反复点头的人。

entries.definition: An old informal word for the head; it only looks like nod and has a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 「脑袋」的古老口语说法；只是拼写与 nod 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To bend the upper body forward as a greeting or sign of respect.
entries.definitionCN: 上身向前弯，表示问候或敬意。

entries.definition: To signal to someone with a movement of the hand or head.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或头的动作示意某人过来。

entries.definition: To sleep lightly for a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 浅浅地睡一小会儿。

entries.definition: A short sleep, usually planned, during the day.
entries.definitionCN: 白天的小睡，通常是有意安排的。

normalIntro.en: The word is probably an expressive gesture word, and its family keeps circling small head movements, approval and sudden sleep.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很可能是模仿动作的表达性词语；词族始终围绕头部的细微动作、许可以及突然的睡意。

normal.en: A nod is one dip and return, unlike a bow, which bends the whole upper body.
normal.cn: 点头只是一次低头再抬起，与弯下整个上身的鞠躬不同。

normal.en: The past form doubled the final consonant: nod becomes nodded, not noded.
normal.cn: 过去式要双写词尾辅音：nod 变成 nodded，不是 noded。

normal.en: Nod off stretches the gesture into sleep, as if the head dips and never comes back.
normal.cn: nod off 把这个动作拖成了睡眠，好像头低下去就再没抬回来。

normal.en: Get the nod means to be approved or chosen, because approval was once given with a silent nod.
normal.cn: get the nod 表示获准或被选中，因为过去常以一个无声的点头表示同意。

normal.en: A nod to is figurative: the head gesture becomes a sign of respect for something old.
normal.cn: a nod to 是比喻用法：点头这个动作变成了对旧事物的尊重。

abstract.en: A gesture too small for words carries a complete yes, which is why nodding survives in every crowded room.
abstract.cn: 一个小到不需要言语的动作，却承载了完整的「是」，所以点头在每个拥挤的房间里都还活着。

abstract.en: The same downward motion marks both politeness and exhaustion, and the language keeps both in one word.
abstract.cn: 同一个向下的动作，既表示礼貌，也表示疲惫，而语言把它俩留在同一个词里。

abstract.en: Nod is the body answering before the mouth has decided what to say.
abstract.cn: nod 是身体在嘴巴想好说什么之前，先替它作了回答。

examples.en: She nodded when I asked whether she agreed.
examples.cn: 我问她是否同意时，她点了点头。

examples.en: He nodded off during the lecture.
examples.cn: 他在讲座中打起了瞌睡。

examples.en: The director gave the young actor the nod.
examples.cn: 导演点头选中了那位年轻演员。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诺的」——一个点头就是一句「诺，答应你」；记住 nod 是点头。

root: 中古英语 nodden，来源不确定，一般认为与模仿点头动作的表达有关；拉丁语没有可靠的同族词。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是头快速地向下一沉；义项由此分出同意、可数的手势、短暂入睡，以及比喻性的致意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the chin drops and springs straight back to where it was.
core.cn: 核心意象：下巴向下一沉，又立刻弹回原位。

definition_en: making or full of loud sound, lively with many people, or containing unwanted random variation in a signal
core_image: 楼板把脚步和音乐一阵阵送下来
scene: 楼上那户人家的地板从晚饭后就没安静过，脚步和音乐声一直传下来。The upstairs neighbours were noisy again, and the whole floor stayed awake.
sceneCN: 这里 noisy 是「吵闹的」（第 1 个义项：发出扰人的大声响）；句意为楼上的邻居又闹了起来，整层楼都没睡着。图中可辨识物件：楼上亮着的窗、木地板、床头的台灯。

pos.zh: 吵闹的；嘈杂的；热闹的；有噪声的

senses.title: Making or full of loud, disturbing sound
senses.definition: making a lot of loud sound, or filled with sound that disturbs people
senses.definitionCN: 发出很大的声响，或充满扰人的声音
senses.example: The street outside the hotel was noisy all night.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆外面的街道整夜都很吵。
senses.why: The suffix -y turns the noun noise into a quality, so a place or person can be described as carrying that sound wherever it goes.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -y 把名词 noise 变成一种性质，于是一个地方或一个人就被描述成走到哪里都带着这种声音。

senses.title: Lively with many people and sounds
senses.definition: full of people, music and activity in a way that feels lively rather than merely annoying
senses.definitionCN: 人多、有音乐、有活动，气氛活跃，而不只是令人烦躁
senses.example: It was a noisy party, with music and laughter in every room.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个热闹的聚会，每个房间都有音乐和笑声。
senses.why: Loud sound is not always a complaint; when many people gather happily, the same quality becomes a sign of life and energy.
senses.whyCN: 响亮的声音并不总是抱怨的对象；当许多人聚在一起高兴时，同一种性质就成了生气与活力的标志。

senses.title: Containing unwanted random variation
senses.titleCN: 有噪声的；夹杂随机误差的
senses.definition: containing random error or interference that hides the true signal, used of data, images or measurements
senses.definitionCN: 含随机误差或干扰，掩盖了真实信号，用于数据、图像或测量
senses.example: The sensor produced noisy data whenever the motor started.
senses.exampleCN: 马达一启动，传感器就会产生有噪声的数据。
senses.why: In technical use the unwanted sound of everyday life becomes unwanted variation in a signal, and the same word follows the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 在技术语境里，日常生活里不受欢迎的声音变成信号中不受欢迎的波动，同一个词顺着这个比喻继续使用。

intro.en: Noisy is the noun noise plus the adjective ending -y; the deeper origin of noise is uncertain, and a suggested Latin link remains unproved.
intro.cn: noisy 是名词 noise 加形容词词尾 -y；noise 更早的来源不确定，与拉丁语的关联只是一种未获证实的猜测。

items.en: The ultimate source of noise is uncertain; a connection with Latin nausea is often suggested but cannot be confirmed.
items.cn: noise 的最终来源不确定；与拉丁语 nausea 的联系常被提出，却无法确认。

items.en: Old French noise named a quarrel, an outcry or a general din.
items.cn: 古法语 noise 指争吵、喊叫或一片喧闹。

items.en: Middle English took the word as a loud outcry and later narrowed it to unwanted sound.
items.cn: 中古英语借入时指大声喊叫，后来缩小为不受欢迎的声音。

items.en: Noise received the ending -y to form noisy, the adjective of a place or person full of sound.
items.cn: noise 加上词尾 -y 构成 noisy，用来形容充满声音的地方或人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense and adds the technical sense of data disturbed by random error.
items.cn: 现代英语保留日常义，并增加了「数据受随机误差干扰」的技术义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noise family and one word that merely resembles it; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for high or overwhelming sound.
note.cn: 形近组收 noise 词族，另收一个只是形似的词；近义组收表示音量大或压倒性声响的形容词。

entries.definition: In a noisy manner; the adverb built from noisy.

entries.definition: Producing a lot of sound; the plain adjective without the sense of disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 发出很大声音的；不带「扰人」意味的一般说法。

entries.definitionCN: 吵闹而粗野、缺乏秩序的。

entries.definition: So loud that it seems to block out every other sound.

entries.definition: Full of loud and continuous demands or shouts.
entries.definitionCN: 充满响亮而持续的要求或呼喊的。

normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 noise 加 -y，词族不断把同一种性质从一个房间延伸到一场聚会，再延伸到一段信号。

normal.en: Noisy describes a noun, while noisily describes how a verb is done.
normal.cn: noisy 修饰名词，noisily 则说明动词是怎么做的。

normal.en: A noisy party is not an insult: the same word can signal fun instead of disturbance.
normal.cn: 说一个聚会 noisy 并不是贬义：同一个词也能表示热闹好玩。

normal.en: In science, noisy data means measurements spoilt by random variation, not by actual sound.
normal.cn: 在科学语境里，noisy data 指被随机波动破坏的测量，而不是真的有声音。

abstract.en: A quality of sound becomes a description of a place, then of a mood, then of a measurement.
abstract.cn: 声音的一种性质，先变成对地方的描述，再变成对气氛的描述，最后变成对测量的描述。

abstract.en: The word shows how easily a nuisance turns into a sign of life, depending on who is listening.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明，同一件扰人的事多么容易变成生命力的标志，全看听的人是谁。

abstract.en: Noisy is the sound of a building with all its windows lit.

intro.cn: 这个词是 noise 加 -y，词族不断在「不受欢迎的声音」这个词根上添加词尾与复合成分。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded; the old suggestion of a link with Latin nausea has never been confirmed.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；关于它与拉丁语 nausea 有关联的旧说法从未得到确认。

发声物品；制造响声的人

definition_zh: 没有一个；一点也没有；没有人；没有一件东西
definition_en: not one and not any; no person and no thing at all; also used in fixed phrases meaning nobody except
core_image: 一只空碗倒扣在桌上，碗底一粒米也没有
scene: 雨后的院子里，桌上那只碗倒扣着，碗底干干净净。None of the seats in the hall had been reserved.
sceneCN: 这里 none 是「没有一个」（第 1 个义项：数量上一点也没有）；句意是大厅里的座位一个也没有被预订。图中可辨识物件：倒扣的碗、空桌、雨后的院子。

pos.zh: 没有一个；一点也没有；没有人

derivatives.zh: 由 no 与 thing 复合而成，义为「没有什么」
由 no 与 body 复合而成，义为「没有人」
由 none、the、less 三部分组合而成，义为「尽管如此」
由同一个古英语否定词简化而来，义为「没有」

senses.title: Not any amount or number of something
senses.definition: not any quantity or number of a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 某一事物的任何数量或数目都不存在
senses.example: None of the milk in the fridge was still fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里的牛奶没有一瓶还是新鲜的。
senses.why: The word began as a compressed phrase meaning not one, so its first job is to deny even the smallest unit of whatever is being counted.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是「不是一个」的压缩说法，所以它最初的本职就是连所数之物的最小单位也一并否认。

senses.title: Not a single person
senses.definition: no person at all in a group that has just been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚提到的那群人中一个也没有
senses.example: None of the neighbours heard the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居中没有一个人听到警报。
senses.why: Because people can be counted one by one like objects, the same denial of a single unit slides from things to persons without a new word being coined.
senses.whyCN: 因为人可以像东西一样一个个数，同一个「连一个都不」的否认就从物滑到人身上，不必另造新词。

senses.title: No thing of the needed kind
senses.definition: no thing at all of the kind that is wanted or expected
senses.definitionCN: 想要或期待的那类东西一件也不存在
senses.example: I asked for a spare key, but there was none.
senses.exampleCN: 我想找一把备用钥匙，却一把也没有。
senses.why: When the group is left unspoken, the word stands alone, and standing alone it simply reports that nothing of the needed kind is there.
senses.whyCN: 当所指的那一组被省略不说，这个词就独自站住；独自站住时，它只报告需要的那类东西一件也不在。

senses.title: Nobody except; only
senses.definition: used in the phrase none but to mean no person except the one named
senses.definitionCN: 用于 none but 这一说法，表示除所说的那一个之外再无别人
senses.example: None but the captain knew the full route.
senses.exampleCN: 除了船长，没有人知道完整航线。
senses.why: The phrase none but first clears away everyone else and then admits a single exception, so a total denial turns into the narrowest possible only.
senses.whyCN: none but 这个说法先把其余人全部清走，再放进唯一的例外，于是彻底的否认转成了范围最窄的「只有」。

intro.en: None is an Old English fusion of a negative particle and the number one, and its whole history is visible in that join.
intro.cn: none 是古英语里否定小词与数词「一」的融合，它的整段历史都写在这个接合处。

items.en: The negative element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic particle of denial, usually written ne, which also stands behind English no and not.
items.cn: 这个否定成分可上溯到一个通常写作 ne 的日耳曼语重构否定小词，英语的 no 与 not 也由它而来。

items.en: Nān was built from ne, not, and ān, one, and it meant not one, already covering both quantities and persons.
items.cn: nān 由 ne（不）与 ān（一）构成，意为「不是一个」，当时已同时覆盖数量和人。

items.en: Middle English kept the word as noon and none, and the form none won out in the written language.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个词写作 noon 与 none 两种形式，最后 none 在书面语中胜出。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the spelling was fixed as none, and the phrase none but was already used for the single exception.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，拼写固定为 none，而 none but 这一说法已用来指唯一的例外。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for quantities, for people and for absent things, while the old link with one survives only in its spelling history.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指数量、指人、也指不在场的东西，而它与 one 的古老联系只留在拼写史里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the negative family built from the same Old English pieces; the near-meaning group collects other words for nothing at all.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一批古英语构件搭成的否定词族；近义组收其他表示「一点也没有」的词。

entries.definition: The negative determiner placed before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 放在名词前的否定限定词。

entries.definitionCN: 一个人也没有。

entries.definition: Not a single thing.
entries.definitionCN: 一样东西也没有。

entries.definitionCN: 旧词后半部分所指的那个数目「一」。

entries.definition: The amount that is lower than any other.
entries.definitionCN: 比任何量都低的量；零。

entries.definition: Nothing at all, especially in scores and accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 一点也没有，尤用于比分和账目。

entries.definition: Nothing whatsoever, used informally.
entries.definitionCN: 一点也没有，非正式说法。

entries.definition: The figure zero, or nothing at all.
entries.definitionCN: 数字零，或一点也没有。

normalIntro.en: The word is a fusion of ne, not, and ān, one, so every sense still carries the ghost of a denied unit.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 ne（不）与 ān（一）的融合，所以每个义项里都还带着一个被否认的单位的影子。

normal.en: The word is a fusion of ne, not, and ān, one, so it literally says not one.
normal.cn: 这个词是 ne（不）与 ān（一）的融合，字面上说的就是「不是一个」。

normal.en: The one inside the word is the same word as the number one, which is why the spelling looks like no plus one.
normal.cn: 词里的 ān 就是数词「一」，所以拼写看起来像 no 加 one。

normal.en: None of takes a singular or a plural noun depending on what is being counted.
normal.cn: none of 后面接单数还是复数，取决于所数的是什么。

normal.en: None but and none other than narrow the field down to a single exception.
normal.cn: none but 与 none other than 把范围收窄到唯一的例外。

normal.en: Nobody and nothing were built the same way, by putting a negative before a general noun.
normal.cn: nobody 与 nothing 用的是同一种造法：在泛指名词前放一个否定成分。

abstract.en: A word made by saying not one reminds us that English often builds a total denial out of the smallest possible unit.
abstract.cn: 一个靠说「不是一个」造出来的词提醒人：英语常拿最小的单位来搭出彻底的否认。

abstract.en: Standing alone, the word turns a missing thing into a subject of its own, so absence can be spoken of as if it were present.
abstract.cn: 独自站住时，这个词把缺席的东西变成自己的主语，于是「没有」也能像在场一样被谈论。

abstract.en: Because it denies a count rather than a quality, it fits things, people and empty places without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 因为它否认的是数目而不是性质，所以它不必变形就能套用于物、人和空处。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a denied single unit; it divides into a denial of quantity, of persons, of available things and of everyone but one exception.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是被否认的单个单位；由此分出对数量的否认、对人的否认、对现有之物的否认，以及对「除一个例外之外所有人」的否认。

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English negative particle, the numeral one and the fused pronoun they produced, with a small family of English compounds around it.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语否定小词、数词「一」以及二者融合出的代词支撑，周围还有一小族英语复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic and has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin non and nullus are different formations rather than the source of this pronoun.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语本族词，没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 non 与 nullus 是另一些构造，而不是这个代词的来源。

items.meaning: not any, no person or thing

items.meaningCN: 不（与目标词拼写相近，词源不同）

definition_zh: 也不；也没有；既不……也不
definition_en: and not; used to join a second negative word or clause, especially after neither or not
core_image: 两扇门并排关着，左边一把锁，右边也一把锁
scene: 仓库两扇门都上了锁，左边一把，右边一把。Neither the driver nor the guard saw the signal.
sceneCN: 这里 nor 是「也不」（第 1 个义项：与 neither 搭配，连接两个都被否定的选项）；句意是司机和警卫都没有看见信号。图中可辨识物件：两扇门、两把锁。

derivatives.zh: 与 nor 配对的否定连词，源自古英语 nāwðer，义为「两者都不」
中古英语形式，nor 的前身，义为「也不」
与 nor 出自同一个古英语词 hwæðer，义为「两者之一」

senses.title: Joining two denied alternatives after neither
senses.definition: used with neither to connect two words or phrases that are both denied
senses.definitionCN: 与 neither 搭配，连接两个都被否定的词或短语
senses.example: Neither the driver nor the guard saw the signal.
senses.exampleCN: 司机和警卫都没有看见信号。
senses.why: The word began as a compressed not either, so its central task is to add a second denied choice after the first has already been ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是「也不」的压缩说法，所以它的核心任务是在第一个选项已被排除之后，再补上一个同样被否定的选项。

senses.title: Adding a negative clause after not, with the verb inverted
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to add another negative clause, usually with the auxiliary before the subject
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定陈述之后，再补一个否定从句，通常把助动词提到主语前面
senses.example: She did not answer, nor did she look up.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有回答，也没有抬头。
senses.why: When two negative statements stand side by side, the second borrows this word, and English marks the link by putting the auxiliary first.
senses.whyCN: 当两个否定陈述并排时，第二个就借用这个词，英语再把助动词提到主语前，以标出这层连接。

senses.title: Literary double use, nor joined to nor
senses.titleCN: 也不……也不（书面重复用法）
senses.definition: used twice in formal or poetic writing to exclude two items with doubled emphasis, without neither
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或诗体文字里连用两次，以加倍的强调排除两个项目，而不借助 neither
senses.example: Nor food nor shelter did they give him.
senses.exampleCN: 他们既没给他食物，也没给他住处。
senses.why: Poets and older writers could repeat the word on both sides, doubling the denial for emphasis instead of leaning on neither.
senses.whyCN: 诗人和旧时作者会把这个词在两边各用一次，用重复来加强否定，而不必依赖 neither。

intro.en: Nor is a clipped Old English pronoun-conjunction meaning not either, reshaped in Middle English and fixed by the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: nor 是一个意为「也不」的古英语代词性连词削短而来，中古英语里经过改形，到十四世纪定形。

items.en: Nāwðer was built from nā, never or no, and hwæðer, which of two, and it meant not either of the two.
items.cn: nāwðer 由 nā（从不、不）与 hwæðer（两者中的哪一个）构成，意为「两者之中哪一个都不」。

items.en: Middle English shortened the word to nother, still meaning not either, and it was often paired with other negatives.
items.cn: 中古英语把词缩成 nother，仍表示「哪一个也不」，并常与其他否定词连用。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the written form nor appeared, generally explained as nother trimmed under the influence of or.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，书面形式 nor 出现，一般认为这是 nother 在 or 的影响下被削短的结果。

items.en: Nor spread first in paired constructions and then in clauses after a negative, while neither kept the fuller role.
items.cn: nor 先在成对结构里流行，随后用于否定句之后的从句，而 neither 保留了更完整的分工。

items.en: Modern English uses nor after neither, after not, and in literary double negatives, though everyday speech often prefers not either.
items.cn: 现代英语在 neither 之后、not 之后以及书面的双重否定里用 nor，不过日常口语常更爱说 not either。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the paired negative word, its older form and the alternative conjunction it is often set against; the near-meaning group collects plainer ways of adding a second denial.
note.cn: 形近组收与它配对的否定词、它的旧形式，以及常与它对照的选择连词；近义组收更朴素的「再加一层否定」说法。

entries.definition: The paired negative word that excludes both of two alternatives.

entries.definitionCN: 表示肯定选择的连词，常出现在同一类句型里，来源与此词不同。

entries.definition: The plain negative adverb used to deny a word or a clause.
entries.definitionCN: 用于否定一个词或一个从句的普通否定副词。

entries.definition: A phrase that adds a second denied item in ordinary speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中再补上一个被否定项的短语。

entries.definition: The everyday spoken way of adding a second negative.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中补上第二个否定项的常用说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is a clipped form of a Germanic negative meaning not either, and its whole life has been spent arriving second.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个意为「也不」的日耳曼语否定词的削短形式，它的一生都在充当第二个到场的否定。

normal.en: Nor is a trimmed form of an Old English word that meant not either of the two.
normal.cn: nor 是一个古英语词的削短形式，那词意为「两者中哪一个也不」。

normal.en: Neither keeps the paired frame, and nor supplies the second half of it.
normal.cn: neither 撑起成对的框架，nor 提供后半截。

normal.en: After not, the auxiliary moves in front of the subject, as in nor did she.
normal.cn: 在 not 之后，助动词移到主语前面，如 nor did she。

normal.en: The word is a conjunction, so it never takes an -s or an -ed ending.
normal.cn: 这个词是连词，所以从不加 -s 或 -ed 词尾。

normal.en: Everyday English often replaces it with not either, while formal writing keeps nor.
normal.cn: 日常英语常用 not either 代替它，正式书面语则保留 nor。

abstract.en: A word made by clipping two negatives into one shows how speech saves effort while keeping the denial.
abstract.cn: 一个把两重否定削成一个的词，说明口语如何在保留否定的同时省力。

abstract.en: Nor always arrives second, which is why it feels like an echo rather than a fresh claim.
abstract.cn: nor 总是第二个到场，所以它听起来像回声，而不像新的主张。

abstract.en: Its survival in formal prose is a small sign of how written English keeps structures that speech has already dropped.
abstract.cn: 它在正式散文里的存活，是书面英语保留口语早已丢掉的结构的微小迹象。

senses.title: The Square Says Yes: conforming to the rule
senses.definition: typical, common, or in accordance with an established standard
senses.definitionCN: 典型的、常见的，或符合既定标准的
senses.example: The machine was running at normal speed.
senses.exampleCN: 机器以正常速度运转。
senses.why: Late Latin normalis meant 'in conformity with rule' and classical Latin described something 'made according to a carpenter's square'. What the square accepts is normal; what it rejects is not.

senses.title: The Right Angle: perpendicular in geometry

senses.example: The normal line meets the curve at exactly ninety degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 法线与曲线恰好成九十度相交。
senses.why: A carpenter's square exists to make right angles. The 1640s geometry sense simply states the tool's job in mathematical language: a normal line is square to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 木工尺存在的目的就是做出直角。17 世纪 40 年代的几何义只是用数学语言说出这件工具的职责：法线与面成直角。

senses.title: Business as Usual: the ordinary standard
senses.definition: conforming to common standards or the established order of things
senses.definitionCN: 符合通行标准或事物的既定秩序
senses.example: Normal service resumed after the power cut.
senses.exampleCN: 停电之后服务恢复正常。
senses.why: Once the square stands for the established order, anything that follows that order is normal. The 1828 sense generalizes the geometrical rule into everyday standards.
senses.whyCN: 当尺子代表既定秩序，任何顺着这个秩序的东西就是 normal。1828 年的义项把几何规矩推广为日常标准。

senses.title: Within the Healthy Range
senses.definition: healthy or functioning within the expected range, used of bodies and body readings
senses.definitionCN: 健康或在预期范围内运作，用于身体及各项读数
senses.example: Her blood pressure was normal for her age.
senses.exampleCN: 就她的年龄而言，血压正常。
senses.why: Medicine measures a body against a range taken from healthy people. A reading inside that range conforms to the rule, so it is called normal.
senses.whyCN: 医学用取自健康人群的范围来量身体。落在这个范围内的读数合乎规矩，于是被称作正常。

senses.title: The Bell Curve: statistically typical
senses.titleCN: 钟形曲线：统计上的典型
senses.definition: falling at or near the average of a statistical distribution
senses.definitionCN: 位于统计分布的均值处或附近
senses.example: Most measurements cluster around the normal value.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数测量值聚集在正常值附近。
senses.why: Statistics turns the rule into a curve: most cases pile up at the middle, and that middle is the normal value. Being near it is being typical.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把规矩变成一条曲线：多数个案堆在中间，中间就是正常值。靠近它就是典型。

senses.title: Nothing Special: ordinary and unremarkable
senses.titleCN: 没有什么特别：普通平常
senses.definition: ordinary and not special or surprising, used of events and days
senses.definitionCN: 普通、不特别也不令人意外的，用于事件和日子
senses.example: It was a normal Tuesday, with nothing unusual at all.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个平常的星期二，没有任何异常。
senses.why: The standard case is also the unexciting case. When nothing departs from the rule, the day is merely normal.
senses.whyCN: 标准情形也是不起眼的情形。当没有任何东西偏离规矩，这一天就只是 normal。

senses.title: Back to Normal: the usual state
senses.definition: the usual or expected state of affairs, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 通常或预期的事态，作名词使用
senses.example: After the storm, the town slowly returned to normal.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，小镇慢慢恢复了常态。
senses.why: The adjective was turned into a noun in 1890: 'the normal' is the state that conforms to the rule. To return to normal is to line up with the square again.
senses.whyCN: 1890 年形容词转为名词：the normal 就是合乎规矩的状态。return to normal 就是重新与尺子对齐。

senses.title: The Perpendicular Line: a geometric noun
senses.definition: a line or plane perpendicular to a given line, surface, or curve
senses.definitionCN: 与给定直线、平面或曲线垂直的线或面
senses.example: Drop a normal from the point to the base line.
senses.exampleCN: 从该点向基线作一条法线。
senses.why: The noun use of 1727 names the very line the square draws. A normal is the line that stands at a right angle, the geometric object behind the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 1727 年的名词用法命名的正是尺子画出的那条线。normal 就是那条成直角的线，是形容词背后的几何对象。

senses.title: The Standard-Setting School
senses.titleCN: 立标准的学校：师范学校
senses.definition: in normal school, a 19th-century teacher-training institution whose name meant 'setting the standard'
senses.definitionCN: normal school 指 19 世纪的师范学校，其名称理据是“用来设定标准的”
senses.example: The state opened its first normal school in 1839.
senses.exampleCN: 该州于 1839 年开办了第一所师范学校。
senses.why: Normal school was translated in 1835 from French école normale (1794). The school was named as the place that sets the standard for teachers, not as a place for 'ordinary' students.
senses.whyCN: normal school 于 1835 年译自法语 école normale（1794）。这所学校被命名为“为教师立标准的地方”，而不是“普通学生的地方”。

intro.en: Normal shares norma with norm, but it appeared much earlier and first meant 'conforming to rule' before it meant 'usual'. The geometrical sense came in the 1640s; the everyday sense 'standard, ordinary' is recorded in 1828.
intro.cn: normal 与 norm 同出 norma，但它出现得早得多，且先有“合乎规矩”义，后有“正常、通常”义。几何义出现于 17 世纪 40 年代；日常的“标准、普通”义记录于 1828 年。

items.en: First recorded with the sense 'typical, common', already applied to ordinary cases rather than to geometry.
items.cn: 最早记录的义项是“典型的、常见的”，已经用于普通情形，而不是几何。

items.en: The geometrical sense 'standing at a right angle, perpendicular' appears, drawing directly on the carpenter's square.
items.cn: 出现几何义“成直角的、垂直的”，直接取象于木工尺。

items.en: From Late Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule, normal'; in classical Latin the same word meant 'made according to a carpenter's square', from norma 'rule, pattern'.
items.cn: 来自晚期拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的、正常的”；古典拉丁语中这个词意为“按木工尺做成的”，出自 norma“规矩、范式”。

items.en: The sense 'conforming to common standards or established order' is recorded, possibly current earlier.
items.cn: 记录到“符合通行标准或既定秩序”的义项，可能在实际使用中更早。

items.en: Normal school is translated from French école normale (1794); the name means an institution that sets the standard.
items.cn: normal school 译自法语 école normale（1794）；这个名字的意思是“设定标准的机构”。

items.en: The noun 'normal state' is recorded in 1890, while the geometrical noun normal 'perpendicular line' dates from 1727. Both keep the image of a line drawn square to something.
items.cn: 名词“常态”记录于 1890 年，而几何名词 normal“垂直线”始于 1727 年。两者都保留了“与某物成直角的一条线”的意象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the same norma family; the near-meaning group holds words that overlap with only part of normal.
note.cn: 形近组是同一个 norma 词族；近义组是只与 normal 部分义项重叠的词。

entries.definition: the standard itself. Normal is the adjective saying that something conforms to it.
entries.definitionCN: 标准本身。normal 是形容词，表示某物合乎这个标准。

entries.definition: prescribing what should be done, not describing what is usual. Normal describes fact; normative sets a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 规定应该怎么做，而不是描述通常怎样。normal 描述事实，normative 立规矩。

entries.definition: departing from the normal. The ab- prefix means 'away from', the exact opposite of conforming.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离正常的。前缀 ab- 意为“离开”，正是“合乎”的反面。

entries.definition: not special or unusual. It stresses lack of distinction, while normal stresses conformity to a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 不特别、不稀奇。它强调“不出众”，normal 强调“合乎标准”。

entries.definition: showing the usual qualities of a group. It points to a representative example, not to a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 体现某类事物通常特征的。它指向代表性样本，而不是规矩。

entries.definition: an established level or rule. It is the noun behind normal; normal is what meets that level.
entries.definitionCN: 既定的水平或规则。它是 normal 背后的名词；normal 就是达到该水平的。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: normal and norm both come from norma, the carpenter's square, and the geometry sense still shows the tool at work.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想是真实的：normal 与 norm 都出自 norma（木工尺），而几何义至今仍能看出这件工具在工作。

normal.en: Normalis in Late Latin meant 'in conformity with rule'; the rule was norma, the carpenter's square.
normal.cn: 晚期拉丁语 normalis 意为“合乎规矩”，而规矩就是 norma，那把木工尺。

normal.en: Normal and norm share norma, but normal is older and started from 'conforming to rule', not from 'usual'.
normal.cn: normal 与 norm 共用 norma，但 normal 更早，而且起点是“合乎规矩”，不是“通常”。

normal.en: In geometry a normal line is square to a surface: the tool's right angle turned into a line.
normal.cn: 几何中的法线与面成直角：工具的直角变成了一条线。

normal.en: Return to normal is a fixed phrase: the state that lines up with the square again.
normal.cn: return to normal 是固定说法：重新与尺子对齐的状态。

normal.en: A normal school was a standard-setting school for teachers, not a school for ordinary people.
normal.cn: normal school 是为教师立标准的学校，不是给普通人办的学校。

abstract.en: Picture a level on a wall: the bubble sits in the middle and the wall is declared true.
abstract.cn: 想象一把水平尺贴在墙上：气泡停在中间，这堵墙就被判为端正。

abstract.en: The same middle position becomes health: a reading inside the expected range is normal.
abstract.cn: 同一个中间位置变成健康：落在预期范围内的读数就是正常。

abstract.en: Move the frame to a crowd and the middle becomes the average person; normal is the crowd's centre line.
abstract.cn: 把框架移到人群，中间就成了平均人；normal 就是人群的中心线。

examples.en: Under normal circumstances, the ferry crosses the river every hour.
examples.cn: 正常情况下，渡轮每小时过河一次。

examples.en: The doctor said the results were normal and no treatment was needed.
examples.cn: 医生说结果正常，不需要治疗。

examples.en: It took three days for the airport to return to normal after the snow.
examples.cn: 大雪过后机场用了三天才恢复正常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺默」——大家都点头应“诺”、默认照做 → normal 正常的、标准的

root: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩的”，出自 norma“木工尺、规矩”；与 norm 同源，先有“合乎规矩”，后有“正常、通常”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of normal all come from one act: laying a square against something. Wood, walls, bodies, numbers and schools are each checked against a rule, and whatever fits is called normal.
sensesIntro.cn: normal 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子贴在某物上。木头、墙壁、身体、数字和学校都要对着规矩检查，对得上的就叫 normal。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a level or square laid against a surface, with no tilt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把水平尺或直角尺贴在表面上，没有倾斜。

branches.en: CONFORMITY: fitting the rule, then fitting the ordinary order of things.
branches.cn: 合乎：先合乎规矩，再合乎事物的日常秩序。

branches.en: GEOMETRY: the perpendicular direction and the perpendicular line itself.
branches.cn: 几何：垂直方向，以及垂直线本身。

branches.en: MEASURED BODIES AND NUMBERS: the healthy range and the centre of a distribution.
branches.cn: 被量度的身体与数字：健康范围与分布中心。

branches.en: THE UNREMARKABLE AND THE USUAL STATE: an ordinary day, and 'the normal' as a noun.
branches.cn: 平常与常态：普通的一天，以及名词 the normal。

branches.en: THE STANDARD-SETTING SCHOOL: normal school, named for the standard it sets.
branches.cn: 立标准的学校：normal school，因它所设定的标准而得名。

intro.en: Normal is norma plus the adjective suffix -alis, which becomes -al in English. The family then adds -ly, -ity, -ize and the negative prefix ab-.
intro.cn: normal 是 norma 加形容词后缀 -alis（进入英语作 -al）。词族随后再加 -ly、-ity、-ize 以及否定前缀 ab-。

latinIntro.en: Latin normalis 'in conformity with rule' comes from norma 'carpenter's square'. Its opposite branch is enormis 'out of rule', and the bare noun norma also gives English norm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 normalis“合乎规矩”出自 norma“木工尺”。它的反义分支是 enormis“出了规矩”，而光秃名词 norma 也给了英语 norm。

items.meaningCN: 正常的；合乎通常标准的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: Normal weather returned after the cold spell.
items.exampleCN: 寒潮过后恢复了正常天气。

items.meaningCN: 通常；正常地（-ly 构成副词）
正常；常态（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The city slowly regained a sense of normality.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市慢慢恢复了常态感。

items.meaningCN: 使正常化；使标准化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The agreement aimed to normalize diplomatic ties.
items.exampleCN: 这项协议旨在使外交关系正常化。

items.meaningCN: 正常化；标准化（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.exampleCN: 数据库规范化减少了重复数据。

items.meaningCN: 规范的；标准性的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: Normative grammar states how people should write.
items.exampleCN: 规范语法说明人们应该怎么写。

items.meaningCN: 异常的；不正常的（ab-“离开”+ normal）
items.example: The test found an abnormal rhythm in the heart.

items.meaningCN: 异常；反常（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: The technicians looked for any abnormality in the sample.
items.exampleCN: 技术人员检查样本中是否有异常。

items.meaningCN: 规范；常态（拉丁名词原样进入英语）
items.example: Late arrival is the norm on rainy days.

items.meaning: literally out of rule; very large
items.meaningCN: 字面“出了规矩”；巨大的（e- 即 ex-“出”）
items.example: The stadium holds an enormous crowd.
items.exampleCN: 这座体育场能容纳极大的人群。

latinEntries.meaning: in conformity with rule; made according to a square
latinEntries.meaningCN: 合乎规矩的；按木工尺做成的
木工尺；规矩；标准（更深来源不确定）
出了规矩的；不规则的；极大的

definition_zh: 通常；正常地；在正常情况下；一般说来
definition_en: usually or in most cases; in the ordinary or expected way; in a healthy physical state rather than an abnormal one
core_image: 一根竖杆稳稳立在底座上，左右两根绳拉得一样直
scene: 脚手架上的竖杆被重新校直，左右两根绳拉成一条线。The pump was repaired and is now running normally.
sceneCN: 这里 normally 是「正常地」（第 2 个义项：按正常方式运转）；句意是水泵修好之后现在运转正常。图中可辨识物件：竖杆、底座、两条拉绳。

pos.zh: 通常；正常地；在正常情况下

derivatives.zh: normally 的基础形容词，源自拉丁语 normalis（合乎矩尺的），义为「正常的；普通的」
由 normal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「正常状态」
由 normal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使正常化」
由 ab-（离开）与 normal 构成，义为「反常的；异常的」

senses.title: In most cases; usually
senses.definition: in most situations or on most occasions
senses.definitionCN: 在多数情形下或多数场合中
senses.example: Normally, the shop closes at six.
senses.exampleCN: 通常这家店六点关门。
senses.why: The adverb comes from an adjective that meant square and true, and applying that to events yields the plain claim that things follow their usual line.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自一个本义为「方正、合乎规矩」的形容词；把它用到事情上，就得出「事情照常走」的平实说法。

senses.title: In the ordinary or expected way
senses.definition: in the way that is expected or that works correctly, without fault or exception
senses.definitionCN: 以符合预期或能正确运作的方式，没有故障或例外
senses.example: The lift is working normally again.
senses.exampleCN: 电梯又恢复正常运行了。
senses.why: If something follows its own rule, it behaves as it should, so the same word moves from how often things happen to how they work.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西若照自己的规矩走，就是按应有的方式运作，于是同一个词从「事情多久发生一次」转到「事情怎么运作」。

senses.title: In a healthy physical state
senses.definition: in a normal physical or medical condition, not diseased or disordered
senses.definitionCN: 处于正常的身体或医学状态，没有病变或紊乱
senses.example: Her heart was beating normally after the rest.
senses.exampleCN: 休息之后她的心跳恢复了正常。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the word because health is defined by the body following its own rule, so a normal reading is one that matches the standard.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了这个词，因为健康本就以身体照自己的规矩运行为准，所以正常的读数就是与标准相符的那个。

senses.title: As one would expect if nothing interferes
senses.definition: used to say what should happen when no unusual event gets in the way
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明在没有意外事件妨碍时事情本应怎样
senses.example: Normally, the train would have arrived by now.
senses.exampleCN: 按说火车这会儿已经到了。
senses.why: The word can also open a sentence and set accidents aside, describing the course events take when nothing bends them away from the rule.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能放在句首，把意外搁到一边，描述在没有外力使事物偏离规矩时它会走的那条路。

intro.en: Normally is the English adverb of normal, a Latin word for a carpenter's square that became the name of everything regular.
intro.cn: normally 是 normal 的英语副词；normal 这个拉丁词本指木匠的矩尺，后来成了「一切合规矩之物」的名称。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square, the tool used to check a right angle, and it already carried the idea of a rule.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的矩尺，用来检查直角，本身已带有「规矩、标准」的意思。

items.en: Normalis meant made according to the square, hence regular and in proper order.
items.cn: normalis 意为按矩尺做成的，因此是「合乎规矩、秩序端正」的。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the seventeenth century, first for things built to a rule and later for what is usual.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个形容词，先指按规矩做成的东西，后来指通常的、普通的。

items.en: The adverb was formed by adding -ly, and it spread in the nineteenth century with the rise of statistics and standard measures.
items.cn: 这个副词由加 -ly 构成，随着统计学和标准计量的兴起在十九世纪流行开来。

items.en: Modern English uses it for what usually happens, for how a machine works and for a healthy bodily state.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指通常发生的事、机器运转的方式，以及健康的身体状态。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the adjective, its derived nouns and verbs, and the word for departure from the rule; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of usual occurrence.
note.cn: 形近组收这个形容词、由它派生的名词与动词，以及表示偏离规矩的词；近义组收其他表示「通常发生」的副词。

entries.definition: Usual, regular, or in proper order.
entries.definitionCN: 通常的、有规律的，或秩序端正的。

entries.definition: The state of being usual or free from disorder.
entries.definitionCN: 处于通常状态或没有紊乱的状态。

entries.definition: To make something regular or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物合乎常规或标准。

entries.definition: Departing from what is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离通常或预期情况的。

entries.definition: On most occasions, as a general rule.
entries.definitionCN: 在多数场合，作为一般规律。

entries.definition: In the ordinary course of things.
entries.definitionCN: 在事情通常的发展过程中。

entries.definition: Frequently, or by most people.
entries.definitionCN: 经常地，或由多数人来做地。

entries.definition: In the way that is characteristic of a kind.
entries.definitionCN: 以某一类事物典型的方式。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a carpenter's square into everyday life, turning a tool for checking right angles into an adverb for what usually happens.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把木匠的矩尺带进日常生活，把检查直角的工具变成了表示「通常如何」的副词。

normal.en: Latin norma was a carpenter's square, so normal first meant cut to a right angle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 norma 是木匠的矩尺，所以 normal 最初指按直角裁成。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective normal into an adverb without changing its meaning.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 把形容词 normal 变成副词，含义不变。

normal.en: Normally usually sits before the verb, as in it normally works.
normal.cn: normally 常放在动词前，如 it normally works。

normal.en: In statistics a normally distributed quantity follows the bell curve, a direct heir of the word's sense of a standard.
normal.cn: 统计学里正态分布的量顺着钟形曲线，正是这个词「标准」义的直系后代。

normal.en: Abnormal adds a prefix of departure, so the pair marks the line between the rule and the exception.
normal.cn: abnormal 加了一个表示「离开」的前缀，这一对词就标出规矩与例外之间的界线。

abstract.en: A word taken from a tool for measuring right angles now measures ordinary life, which shows how deeply English borrows the workshop for the mind.
abstract.cn: 一个取自量直角工具的借词如今用来衡量日常生活，可见英语向工坊借词借得有多深。

abstract.en: Normally is a quiet promise about the future: it describes the path things take unless something bends them aside.
abstract.cn: normally 是对未来的一句轻声保证：它描述在没有外力把事物掰弯时它们会走的路。

abstract.en: The same adverb covers habit, machinery and health because all three are judged against a rule the thing is expected to follow.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词能覆盖习惯、机器和健康，因为三者都是拿「事物本应遵守的规矩」来评判的。

examples.en: Normally, the shop closes at six.

definition_en: the compass direction opposite to south and toward the North Pole; also the northern part of a country, and a position or movement facing that way
core_image: 指南针的针稳稳指向地图上方，那里的天空发白、风又冷又硬
scene: 清晨的站台上，风向标被风推得直指一侧，等车的人把围巾又绕了一圈。A cold wind came down from the north, and everyone turned their backs to it.
sceneCN: 这里是「北方、北面」（第 1 个义项：罗盘上指向北极的方向），句意为一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。图中可辨识物件：风向标、围巾、站台长椅。

senses.title: The compass direction toward the North Pole
senses.definition: the direction that is opposite to south and points toward the North Pole, one of the four main points of the compass
senses.definitionCN: 与南相反、指向北极的方向，是罗盘上四个主要方位之一
senses.example: A cold wind came down from the north, and everyone turned their backs to it.
senses.exampleCN: 一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。
senses.why: The Old English word named the direction to the left when a person faced the rising sun, and that left-hand side became the fixed compass point we still call north.
senses.whyCN: 古英语这个词命名的是面朝日出时左手边的那一侧，这一侧后来固定成罗盘上的方位，也就是今天的「北」。

senses.title: The northern part of a country or region
senses.definition: the part of a country, region or continent that lies furthest toward the north
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家、地区或大陆中最靠北的那一部分
senses.example: Her family moved to the north after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，她家搬到了北部。
senses.why: Once north names a direction, the land lying in that direction can take the same name, so a country's cold upper half is simply called the north.
senses.whyCN: 既然 north 能指一个方向，位于那个方向上的土地也就用同一个词来称呼，于是一个国家寒冷的上一半就被叫作「北部」。

senses.title: The side or face that points north
senses.definition: the side of a building, hill or object that faces north, often the coolest or most shaded side
senses.definitionCN: 建筑物、山丘或物体朝北的一面，通常也是最凉、最背阴的一面
senses.example: The north face of the house stays in shadow most of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子朝北的一面一天里大部分时间都在阴影里。
senses.why: A direction also marks one face of any object, so north shifted from a point on a map to a particular wall or slope, carrying its cold and shaded quality with it.
senses.whyCN: 方向也标出任何物体的某一个面，于是 north 从地图上的一个点转指某一面墙或某道山坡，同时把寒冷背阴的意味带了进去。

senses.title: Toward the north
senses.definition: in or toward the north, used mainly with verbs of movement
senses.definitionCN: 向北或在北方，主要与表示移动的动词连用
senses.example: They drove north along the coast for three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着海岸向北开了三个小时。
senses.why: Because the word already fixes a destination, English can use it unchanged as an adverb of movement, and no separate form is needed for going that way.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词本身就固定了一个目的地，英语可以直接拿它当表示移动的副词，往那个方向走不必另造形式。

intro.en: North is a native Germanic word whose oldest recorded meaning is the direction on the left when one faces the rising sun; its deeper origin is reconstructed rather than certain.
intro.cn: north 是日耳曼语本土词，最早可考的意思是面朝日出时左手边的那一侧；它更古老的来源属于重构，并不确定。

items.en: A commonly proposed root for this group meant left or below, the side to a person's left when facing the dawn; the reconstruction is uncertain and not accepted by every scholar.
items.cn: 一般认为，这一族词有一个词根表示「左」或「下方」，即面朝晨光时人的左手边；这一重构并不确定，也并非所有学者都接受。

items.en: The Germanic form kept the sense of a left-hand direction and added a comparative ending, so the ancestor of north meant roughly the more leftward side.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式保留了「左手边方向」的意思，并加了一个比较级词尾，因此 north 的祖先大致表示「更靠左的一侧」。

items.en: Norþ was the ordinary word for the direction and also stood in compounds for northern places and peoples.
items.cn: norþ 是表示这个方向的常用词，也出现在指北方地点与部族的复合词里。

items.en: Middle English settled the spelling as north and used it for the compass point, the northern region and the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写固定为 north，并用它表示罗盘方位、北部地区以及形容词。

items.en: Modern English adds the adverb use, the phrase north of, and capitalized names such as the North Pole and the North Sea.
items.cn: 现代英语增添了副词用法、north of 这一说法，以及 North Pole、North Sea 这类首字母大写的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on the same direction word; the near-meaning group puts north against the other compass points and the cold region it names.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在同一个方位词上的词族；近义组把 north 与其他方位词以及它所命名的寒冷地区放在一起对照。

entries.definitionCN: 由 north 加 -ern 构成，义为「北方的；在北部的」。

entries.definitionCN: north 加 -ward，表示朝北移动。

entries.definition: A wind or direction coming from or pointing toward the north.

entries.definition: The compass point directly opposite north, toward the South Pole.
entries.definitionCN: 与 north 正相反、指向南极的罗盘方位。

entries.definition: Of the far north and the cold region around the North Pole.
entries.definitionCN: 指极北地区以及北极圈附近的寒冷地带。

entries.definition: Of the poles, the two ends of the earth's axis where the cold is deepest.
entries.definitionCN: 指地球自转轴两端、最寒冷的极地。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as the left-hand side of the sunrise and ends as a fixed compass point, and every later use keeps that same cold direction.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从日出时的左手边开始，最后固定成罗盘上的一个点，后来的每一种用法都保留着同一个寒冷的方向。

normal.en: Old English norþ named the left side of a person facing the rising sun, so the word's first job was to point at a side of the sky.
normal.cn: 古英语 norþ 指的是面朝日出时人的左手边，所以这个词最初的任务是指向天空的一侧。

normal.en: The Germanic ending on its ancestor was comparative, which is why north can be understood as the more leftward direction.
normal.cn: 它祖先身上的日耳曼语词尾是比较级，所以 north 可以理解为「更靠左的那个方向」。

normal.en: Northern is north plus -ern, a suffix that means belonging to a direction, as in western and southern.
normal.cn: northern 是 north 加 -ern，这个词尾表示「属于某个方向」，western 与 southern 也是这样构成的。

normal.en: Northward adds -ward, the suffix for movement toward a place, so the word itself says going that way.
normal.cn: northward 加了 -ward，这个词尾表示「朝某处移动」，所以词本身就在说「往那边走」。

normal.en: North of is a fixed way to locate a place, as in a village north of the river.
normal.cn: north of 是给地点定位的固定说法，例如「a village north of the river」这样的表达。

abstract.en: A compass point that started as a person's left hand shows how a word can move from the body to the map without changing its meaning.
abstract.cn: 一个从人的左手开始的方位词，展示了词如何从身体移到地图上，而意思并不改变。

abstract.en: Coldness clings to north because the direction itself brings the polar air, so the word carries weather inside its meaning.
abstract.cn: 寒冷一直黏在 north 上，因为那个方向本身就带来极地的空气，这个词把天气装进了自己的意思里。

abstract.en: Every use of north, from a wall to a whole region, is the same arrow pointing at one end of the world.
abstract.cn: north 的每一种用法，从一面墙到一整片地区，都是同一支指向世界一端的箭。

examples.cn: 一股冷风从北面吹来，人们都转过身背对着风。

examples.cn: 村子在河以北，离桥大约一英里。

examples.en: The north face of the house stays in shadow most of the day.
examples.cn: 这栋房子朝北的一面一天里大部分时间都在阴影里。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是指向极地的罗盘方位；义项由此分出某地的北部、物体朝北的一面，以及朝那个方向的移动。
